findings.title: Server-side JavaScript injection via eval() on contribution inputs
findings.attack_path: Authenticated user POSTs preTax/afterTax/roth to /contributions; values pass straight to eval(); attacker supplies a JS payload (e.g. global.process.exit() or a require('child_process') one-liner) achieving arbitrary code execution in the Node process.
findings.remediation: Replace eval() with parseInt(req.body.preTax, 10) and reject NaN, as the commented A1 fix shows.

findings.title: NoSQL JavaScript injection via $where in allocations threshold
findings.attack_path: threshold query param is interpolated into a Mongo {$where: "...this.stocks > '<threshold>'"} string with no validation; payloads like 0';while(true){}' or 1'; return 1 == '1 inject arbitrary JS evaluated by the database, enabling data exfiltration and DoS.
findings.remediation: parseInt the threshold and range-check it; never build $where from user input — use typed comparison operators.

findings.title: Passwords stored and compared in plaintext
findings.attack_path: addUser stores password as-is and validateLogin uses string equality; any DB read (NoSQL injection, backup theft, insider) yields every cleartext credential for immediate reuse.
findings.remediation: Hash with bcrypt.hashSync on signup and bcrypt.compareSync on login (the commented A2 fix).

findings.title: Server-side request forgery in stock research proxy
findings.attack_path: GET /research builds url from req.query.url + req.query.symbol and passes it to needle.get with no allowlist; attacker points it at 169.254.169.254 metadata, internal services, or file/gopher schemes and the response body is echoed back.
findings.remediation: Remove the user-supplied url; pin a fixed provider host, validate symbol, and block internal address ranges.

findings.title: Stored XSS via shared memos with template auto-escaping disabled
findings.attack_path: POST /memos stores req.body.memo unsanitized; getAllMemos returns memos to every user and swig runs with autoescape:false, so a script payload executes in other users' (including admins') sessions — account takeover chain.
findings.remediation: Set swig autoescape:true and contextually encode memo output; scope memo visibility.

findings.title: IDOR: allocations addressed by URL userId
findings.attack_path: displayAllocations reads userId from req.params instead of the session; any authenticated user enumerates /allocations/<n> to read other members' portfolio allocations.
findings.remediation: Derive userId from req.session and ignore the path parameter (the commented A4 fix).

findings.title: Missing function-level access control on benefits administration
findings.attack_path: /benefits is guarded only by isLoggedIn, not isAdmin; the handler hardcodes user.isAdmin=true, so any user lists all non-admin users and rewrites benefitStartDate.
findings.remediation: Add the isAdmin middleware to both /benefits routes (the commented A7 fix).

findings.title: TLS private key and certificate committed to the repository
findings.attack_path: artifacts/cert/server.key holds a usable RSA private key in version control; anyone with repo access can impersonate the TLS endpoint or decrypt captured traffic.
findings.remediation: Remove the key/cert from history, rotate them, and inject certificates from a secrets manager at deploy time.

findings.title: Hardcoded session, crypto, and scanner secrets in config
findings.attack_path: config/env/all.js ships cookieSecret and cryptoKey as fixed strings and the env files commit a ZAP apiKey; a known cookieSecret lets an attacker forge/seal session cookies and a known cryptoKey defeats any field encryption.
findings.remediation: Load all secrets from environment/secret store, generate strong random values per deploy, and remove committed values.

findings.title: Application served over cleartext HTTP
findings.attack_path: server.js starts http.createServer; the HTTPS block is commented out, so credentials, session cookies, and PII traverse the internet edge in plaintext and are sniffable/MITM-able.
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS (the commented HTTPS server), set secure cookies, and add HSTS.

findings.title: Seeded default admin account with weak password
findings.attack_path: db-reset seeds admin/Admin_123 (isAdmin:true) and user1/user2 with guessable passwords; combined with plaintext storage and no lockout, an attacker logs straight in as admin.
findings.remediation: Do not ship default credentials to production; force first-login rotation and seed only in test.

findings.title: Open redirect via /learn url parameter
findings.attack_path: GET /learn calls res.redirect(req.query.url) with no allowlist; attacker crafts a link that bounces victims to a phishing or token-stealing site under the app's domain trust.
findings.remediation: Redirect only to a vetted allowlist of relative paths.

findings.title: Regular expression denial of service in bank-routing validation
findings.attack_path: /profile validates bankRouting with /([0-9]+)+#/ (nested quantifier); a string of digits without a trailing # causes catastrophic backtracking that pins the single-threaded event loop.
findings.remediation: Use the non-nested /([0-9]+)#/ pattern and cap input length.

findings.title: Sensitive PII (SSN, DOB, bank details) stored unencrypted
findings.attack_path: profile-dao stores ssn/dob/bankAcc/bankRouting in plaintext (encryption helpers commented out); any DB compromise discloses full identity/financial records of every member.
findings.remediation: Encrypt SSN/DOB/bank fields at rest with a KMS-managed key (the commented A6 fix) and enforce field-level access.

findings.title: No session regeneration on login; insecure session cookie flags
findings.attack_path: handleLoginRequest sets req.session.userId without regenerate(); session cookie is configured without httpOnly/secure/sameSite, enabling session fixation and theft of the un-flagged cookie over the cleartext channel.
findings.remediation: Call req.session.regenerate() on login and set httpOnly, secure, sameSite=strict cookie options.

findings.title: Username enumeration via distinct login error messages
findings.attack_path: validateLogin returns 'Invalid username' vs 'Invalid password' distinctly, so an attacker harvests valid usernames before credential stuffing.
findings.remediation: Return one generic 'Invalid username and/or password' message for both cases.

findings.title: No CSRF protection on state-changing POST routes
findings.attack_path: csurf middleware is commented out; a logged-in victim visiting a malicious page silently submits /profile, /contributions, /benefits, or /memos changes using their ambient session cookie.
findings.remediation: Enable csurf and embed/verify a CSRF token in every form (the commented A8 fix).

findings.title: Security response headers disabled (clickjacking, MIME sniffing)
findings.attack_path: helmet, frameguard, noSniff, CSP, and HSTS are all commented out and x-powered-by is exposed; the app can be framed for clickjacking and content-type-sniffed.
findings.remediation: Enable helmet with frameguard, noSniff, CSP, HSTS and disable x-powered-by (the commented A5 fix).

findings.title: Log injection / CRLF via unsanitized username in failed-login log
findings.attack_path: console.log writes the raw userName on a bad login; CRLF in the username forges additional log lines, corrupting audit trails or poisoning a downstream log viewer.
findings.remediation: Encode/strip CRLF before logging (the commented ESAPI A1-3 fix).

findings.title: Vulnerable and outdated third-party dependencies
findings.attack_path: package.json pins marked 0.3.5 (XSS-bypass CVEs), swig 1.4.2 (EOL SSTI surface), mongodb 2.x and express 4.13 (EOL); a known exploit in any of these is directly reachable in the running app.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to maintained versions, add npm audit/Snyk to CI, and replace abandoned packages (swig, bcrypt-nodejs).

findings.title: Verbose error handler leaks stack traces to clients
findings.attack_path: errorHandler renders the raw error object (including stack) into error-template, exposing file paths, library versions, and internal logic to aid follow-on attacks.
findings.remediation: Render a generic error page in production; log details server-side only.

findings.title: Weak signup password policy
findings.attack_path: validateSignup PASS_RE is /^.{1,20}$/ — a single character passes; combined with no lockout this enables trivial brute force/credential stuffing.
findings.remediation: Require >=8 chars with mixed classes (the commented stronger PASS_RE) and add rate limiting.

findings.title: NoSQL operator injection on login via untyped request body
findings.attack_path: userName from the JSON body reaches usersCol.findOne({userName}) untyped; a body like {"userName":{"$gt":""}} matches an arbitrary user document, and with plaintext comparison can bypass auth.
findings.remediation: Coerce userName/password to strings before querying and reject non-string types.

kill_chains.goal: Remote code execution and host control
Privilege escalation to admin via stored XSS
Pivot to internal network via SSRF
